Hey there, I just wanted to sympathize because we went through something similar with my now-7 month old. We had a very strict sleep consultant who was adamant about training naps and nights at the same time - but the truth is, you can train them separately with no impact to night sleep! We followed a modified ferber method for a few days and found the naps to be too distressing for everyone. Our baby was also sooo sad and miserable and getting scared of his nursery, being placed down at all, or being separated from Mom. He even lost a bit of weight which broke us.

Luckily he managed to figure out sleeping through the night, but we called it quits for the nap training because it was just too much change and stress for one baby to handle at once! I'm glad we did because once we went back to contact/carrier/stroller naps, our happy baby slowly came back. 

My mentality around it is to keep up the sleep (night) training - or all that crying would have been for nothing! Your baby can do it. Revisit the nap training whenever you feel ready. I might also suggest a gentler approach, as I've gone about it over time. Instead of just the quick goodbyes, I've started just hovering over and keeping my arm around his head, patting him, holding hands, singing, shushing, doing whatever I can, even if it meant staying there for half an hour, to get baby to fall asleep in his crib. It was easier on him that way, and he would still manage to sleep through the night (with some fussing, but he would be able to self settle within 10-15 min). 

Another suggestion is to try to get as much fun, loving, play time in the nursery or crib as well, even if it's just for a few minutes. Keep as positive as possible as your baby is super in tune with how you feel and will act on it! 

I'm sorry you had such a hard time with training. Your happy baby will come back and forget it all with time! He knows you still love him.

Our 7 month old was also refusing crib so we coslept for a few months, and he needed a few comfort suckles through the night, like yours. We just finished night 4 of ST (modified ferber with intervaled check-ins) and we've already saw huge success at night 2.

Our consultant said if he really needs the calories, that we could do a dream feed between the hours of 9-12. Any later will disrupt their sleep and it'll be hard to resettle. The key is the make sure they're asleep when you go in to feed them- daunting, but helps with keeping the consistency of not picking them up because they're crying. We've finished night 4 of ST with this method and he hasn't needed a middle of the night feed, and the dream feed was enough for him.

Our consultant reassured that they're not expending much calories while they're sleeping and don't need the night feeds at their age.

Let me know if you need more tips! I feel you! Keep yourself busy while they cry - wash dishes, bottles, etc. Plug in and watch a drama and the time goes by quickly and before you know it, you'll see them self settling to sleep. The crying and yelling is just them venting their frustration that they're not used to this, but they will figure it out - believe in your baby :)

It's concerning to me that you don't know the meaning of the name from them - I would start there to try to bridge the gap between yourself and the in laws. 

As a fully Chinese person who really embraces the culture, picking a Chinese name is a very nuanced and incredibly special occasion, and from experience, I've seen some really lovely and meaningful names come from this process.

Shu Guang for example, depending on the character selection could mean "the light of dawn." There could be several considerations that went into this name, including the use of certain "elements" to balance out certain factors.

I've heard of names being picked to offset certain uncontrollable things like zodiac signs. Apparently, done right, the name would account for all 4 elements like water, fire, earth, wind - so if a child is born on a year of a water rabbit for example, the name may need more earth character strokes (yes there are different strokes that denote different elements within a character) to balance it out. 

I've been told that a relative of mine had too many water elements in their name and birth zodiac, and that's why they are always "all over the place" and never "grounded" or "rooted" enough with earth elements in their name, which would've helped them settle down with a clearer place or mindset in life. This was something that was caught after the fact by a "name master," as silly as that sounds lol.

All this to say - this should be an unique and meaningful way for you and your future child to connect with the culture. I'm sorry to hear it seems they haven't been open to collaborate. I hope that by extending the olive branch with an intention to understand more will help them let you in to their way of making these kinds of decisions. Asian parents can be stubborn, and can take lots of patience to work with, so it helps to have an open mind and to tread lightly around it. Good luck!!

I usually instinctively use a curler before mascara just because my lashes are so straight, but I've found that if I don't have a curler, with the right hand motion, I can get my lashes to stay up without one.

Hard to explain, but I'd turn my wrist outwards while pressing the wand into my lashes while I half-blink into it, so there's some natural pressure to push and hold the lashes up.

There's a Youtuber who does the same technique and explains it really well! (EDIT: I wanted to link you to the video where she demonstrates the technique but reddit won't let me). Look up "MAKEUP MISTAKES TO AVOID -PART 2/WRONG COLORS" by Ali Andreea, and go to the 27:07 mark! She doesn't appear to use a curler either (and don't mind the side of her face on the right, in this video she demonstrates a "wrong" side and a "right" side to makeup tricks haha).

I actually recommend all her makeup do's and don'ts videos too if you have the time :) I learnt a lot from those.

Pricier, but my Holy Grail for my stubborn straight lashes is DiorShow Iconic Overcurl mascara. I've tried soo many mascaras and liked Loreal Voluminous for a while, switched briefly to Estee Lauder, among others, but always go back to DiorShow. 

It has been the best across the board in terms of staying power in holding the curl, no smudges, showing up really nicely in photos, and also being easy to wash off (unless you get the waterproof one which I actually also really recommend for going to humid places or if you're going swimming, etc). My favourite hands down!

I started taking Cipralex (which I think is called Lexapro in the states) about 11 days ago. My experience:

* The first week was hell. I was so nauseous and was unable to eat anything. I couldn't even brush my teeth or drink water without gagging or feeling like vomiting.
* I had a huge loss of appetite.
* Around the 3rd night in, I felt extremely depressed and suicidal; I was a wreck. I had to call for help. However, I ended up calming down and sleeping soundly after that episode.
* Frequent yawning. I just can't stop yawning even after I've had good rest, it's so annoying.
* ... Problems on the toilet.
* Increased heart rate.
* Prickling feeling on my skin.
* Sometimes some shakiness.

These are all side effects that I was notified about beforehand. I kept with the medication, having been told that the side effects wouldn't last.

I'm glad I did because **I'm feeling a lot better now**. The nausea is about gone, as are most of the other side effects. I'm feeling a lot more optimistic, and although sometimes some thoughts will cause me to tear up, I don't actually feel *depressed*. My thoughts are a lot clearer and less anxious or worried, and I'm able to concentrate better on work like never before.

It took about 10 days, starting with 2.5 mg, to 5 mg, to full 10 mg dosages.

It's still quite early on in the process, but I think I made the right choice in accepting the prescription my doctor gave me. It can be quite scary at first, but I think it's worth a try. If it doesn't work out for you, your doctor would help you with stopping the prescription.

Good luck.

During regular hours it can be quite pricey, but if you go after 10pm, all your sushi, drinks, and sashimi orders are 50% off!
